I've been farming this same land in Quzhou my whole life, just like my father before me. I know this soil, I know this weather, and I know what sells. The answer is the same as every year: **winter wheat followed by summer maize** on the same ground. That's the rotation every family here does, and for good reason.

I have 10 mu of land, nothing wasted. Wheat goes in October and comes off in June. Corn goes straight in after — no waiting, no rest. Two harvests, one piece of ground. Wheat has the government floor price, so I know I won't lose money on it. Corn goes to the local feed traders, price varies but there's always a buyer.

For wheat, I buy improved seeds from the village seed station — not the old landraces, but not the expensive hybrid wheat either. That's not how we do it here. I put down a base of diammonium phosphate and urea before planting, then come back with urea top-dress at jointing. I water four times — before seeding to set the seedbed, over winter to protect the roots, at jointing, and again at heading. Three spray rounds: one herbicide in spring, one for aphids, one preventive fungicide near heading.

For corn, I use Zhengdan 958 hybrid seed. Everyone around here uses it. I direct-seed it right after the wheat comes off — no tillage, just go straight in. Fertilizer at planting, urea top-dress at the six-leaf stage. I only irrigate at planting if it's dry, and once more at tasseling if it hasn't rained. Herbicide right after seeding, maybe one more spray for armyworm if it's a bad year.

I'm not changing what works.
